record.result: A possible approach is to identify a totally disconnected set of Brownian times surviving boundary removal. That would not suffice: the Cantor function restricted to the middle-third Cantor set maps this totally disconnected compact set continuously onto [0,1]. Continuous images can be connected.

record.independent_check: Adjacent vertices cannot both be peaks. In the four-cycle, a proposed peak with label 2 would have to exceed both other nonpeak labels, which is impossible; this checks the count without enumeration software.
record.method: Exact small-grid count and an orientation reformulation
record.obstruction: The small-grid calculation gives no large-n scale. The orientation sum requires sharp weighted counts of acyclic orientations with two prescribed sinks. The source title says repel while its displayed question asks distance/n -> 0; that wording discrepancy is retained, not silently corrected.
record.result: On the 2-by-2 grid (a four-cycle), exactly two peaks must be opposite and carry labels 3 and 4. There are two choices of diagonal, two orders of the top labels, and two orders of the bottom labels: eight of the 24 labelings. Their graph distance is always two. More generally orient each edge toward its larger label. Two peaks means precisely two sinks of the induced acyclic orientation; the number of labelings yielding a fixed orientation is its number of linear extensions.

record.independent_check: Use max_j |Z_j|<=(sum_j |Z_j|^p)^(1/p) and Jensen, then sum the resulting geometric series. The increment bound implies stochastic continuity, identifying the modification at each deterministic point; Fubini identifies it at each independent uniform sample point, and countability handles the entire sampled sequence.

record.obstruction: The source only gives first moments of individual route lengths, not p-moment increments of L. Its compatibility condition does not make Euclidean route length an automatic metric with a triangle inequality, so a metric-chaining shortcut is unjustified.
record.result: Let L(x)=len R(0,x). Suppose on a containing square E|L(x)-L(y)|^p<=C*|x-y|^p for a p>2, with a jointly measurable version and finite mean at one anchor. On the dyadic grid of mesh2^-k there are order2^(2k) parent-child or neighbor pairs. The expected maximum increment is at most Cprime*2^(-k*(1-2/p)). This is summable, so telescoping along grid ancestors constructs a continuous modification with finite expected supremum.
